activation: Client-managed connection; signing enabled; GMAC negotiated; server multichannel capability present. Other authentication paths remain direct.
implemented: Create a private physical bootstrap using the exact caller configuration, event bus, authentication hostname and actual endpoint.
Register it with the SMBClient before connect; explicitly release tracking in finally, including callers with a different event bus.
Authenticate the target session privately and reserve its next native MID for possible original-key abort LOGOFF.
Bind back onto the caller with existing auxiliary authentication and per-request reservation; retain at most 16 sparse initial-caller original-key MIDs.
Publish canonical caller handoff under the client-close gate; ordinary sends use the bound key and do not advance original-key state.
Force-close the private bootstrap without LOGOFF on success; remove it from the shared channel list.
On failed handoff/binding close the unpublished session without closing its borrowed caller, then dispose the owned private root.

reservation_state.initial_prefix: All MIDs consumed by private initial authentication remain burned.
reservation_state.abort_slot: Next private MID is excluded from every candidate and can be claimed once only for original-channel LOGOFF; terminal -1 is rejected.
reservation_state.initial_caller: At most 16 distinct original-key binding request MIDs stored as sparse outliers, serialized by that physical connection allocation lock.
reservation_state.later_bindings: Existing atomic high-water reservation, excluding initial sparse IDs; no release on uncertain outcomes.
reservation_state.wire_sequence: Real unsigned ECHOs consume collisions through native credits and lowest-MID allocation; no counter assignment, skip or rewind.
reservation_state.cost_limit: Application traffic and a busy caller counter do not raise the low reservation cursor. Total catch-up cost can still grow with binding/retry history.
